questions.answer: To provide all nutrients the body needs to grow, work and stay healthy

questions.text: Which meal looks MOST balanced?
options: Two large bowls of rice and a sweet
Roti, dal, vegetable, curd, and salad
Fried snack and a soft drink
questions.answer: Roti, dal, vegetable, curd, and salad
questions.explanation: This thali pattern includes carbs, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre.

questions.text: A child eats only rice and some sugar all day. What is MOST likely to happen?
options: He may not get enough proteins, vitamins, and minerals to grow well
questions.answer: He may not get enough proteins, vitamins, and minerals to grow well
questions.explanation: Such a diet is high in carbs but missing protein, vitamins, and minerals.

questions.text: Which is the MOST important habit for a healthy diet?
options: Eating a variety of fresh foods in moderate amounts
questions.answer: Eating a variety of fresh foods in moderate amounts
questions.explanation: Variety + moderation keeps the diet balanced.

questions.text: Drinking enough water every day is
options: Necessary because the body uses water in many processes
questions.answer: Necessary because the body uses water in many processes
questions.explanation: Water is essential for digestion, transport in blood, and waste removal.

questions.text: Aman wants to eat protein-rich snacks. Which is the BEST choice?
questions.explanation: Eggs and chana (chickpeas) are high in protein.

questions.text: Eating fruits as part of meals helps because fruits provide
questions.explanation: Fruits are good sources of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fibre.

questions.text: Two children eat the same amount of rice every day. One also eats dal, vegetables, and milk. Which child is MORE likely to grow well, and why?
options: The first, because rice has everything
The second, because the extra foods provide proteins, vitamins, and minerals missing from rice
Both equally, because rice is enough
The second, because more food means more weight only
questions.answer: The second, because the extra foods provide proteins, vitamins, and minerals missing from rice
questions.explanation: Rice alone lacks key nutrients; the second child gets a more balanced diet.

questions.text: Which advice is BEST for someone trying to eat 'mindfully'?
options: Chew well, eat slowly, and stop when comfortably full
Eat extra so you don't feel hungry later
questions.answer: Chew well, eat slowly, and stop when comfortably full
questions.explanation: Mindful eating slows you down and helps you notice when you're full.

questions.explanation: Different foods come from plants (grains, fruits) and animals (milk, eggs).

questions.answer: Add a drop of iodine and watch for a blue-black colour

questions.text: Why are fresh fruits and vegetables important?
options: They give vitamins, minerals and fibre
questions.answer: They give vitamins, minerals and fibre
questions.explanation: Fresh fruits and vegetables are rich in protective nutrients.

questions.text: A meal of butter, jam, and white bread provides mostly
options: Carbohydrates and fats but very little protein, vitamins, or fibre
questions.answer: Carbohydrates and fats but very little protein, vitamins, or fibre
questions.explanation: This combination is high in energy but poor in protein and protective nutrients.

questions.text: To make this meal more balanced, the BEST addition would be
options: An egg or paneer and a vegetable like cucumber
questions.answer: An egg or paneer and a vegetable like cucumber
questions.explanation: Adds protein and vitamins/fibre to balance the meal.

questions.text: Why should we wash hands before eating?
options: To remove germs and dirt that could enter the body with the food
questions.answer: To remove germs and dirt that could enter the body with the food
questions.explanation: Hand washing reduces the risk of food-borne illness.

questions.text: Which is a good habit for safe food?
options: Eating cooked food kept in open for many hours
Washing fruits and vegetables before eating
questions.answer: Washing fruits and vegetables before eating
questions.explanation: Washing removes pesticides and dirt.

questions.text: Carbohydrates and fats both provide energy.
questions.explanation: Both are major energy-giving nutrients.

questions.text: Vitamin C deficiency causes goitre.

questions.text: Fibre (roughage) helps in digestion.
questions.explanation: Fibre helps food move through the intestine smoothly.

questions.text: Eating only sweets every day is a balanced diet.
questions.explanation: Sweets give energy but lack proteins, vitamins, minerals, and fibre.

questions.text: Drinking milk regularly helps in building strong bones because milk has calcium.
questions.explanation: Milk is a major source of calcium needed for bone growth.

questions.text: A child suffering from rickets needs more vitamin D and calcium.
questions.explanation: Rickets is treated by adding vitamin D (e.g., sunlight, fortified milk) and calcium.

questions.text: Adding lemon to a meal can help the body absorb iron from spinach.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C (in lemon) helps the body absorb iron better.

questions.text: All fats are bad for health.
questions.explanation: Some fats (like those in nuts and seeds) are needed in moderation; only excess of unhealthy fats is harmful.

questions.text: Skipping breakfast every day is a healthy habit for school children.
questions.explanation: Breakfast supplies energy and concentration for the school day.

questions.text: Carbohydrates give us _____.
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are quick energy sources.

questions.text: Proteins are body-building nutrients found in foods like dal, eggs, and _____.

questions.text: Lack of iron in food can cause the disease called _____.
questions.explanation: Iron deficiency leads to anaemia.

questions.text: Vitamin C deficiency causes the disease called _____.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy.

questions.text: Vitamin D deficiency in children causes _____.
questions.explanation: Lack of vitamin D leads to rickets.

questions.text: Iodine deficiency causes _____.
questions.explanation: Iodine lack leads to goitre, an enlarged thyroid.

questions.text: A diet that has every food group in suitable amounts is called a _____ diet.
questions.explanation: A balanced diet has every nutrient in the right amount.

questions.text: _____ is the indigestible plant material that helps in passing waste smoothly.
questions.explanation: Roughage (fibre) keeps the digestive system moving smoothly.

questions.text: The chemical that turns blue-black with iodine is _____.
questions.explanation: Iodine + starch → blue-black colour.

questions.text: Iron in spinach is absorbed better when eaten with foods that contain vitamin _____.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C boosts iron absorption.

questions.text: A diet low in proteins, vitamins, and minerals leads to a _____ disease.
questions.explanation: Diseases caused by missing nutrients are called deficiency diseases.

questions.text: List the major food groups.
questions.answer: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre (roughage), and water.
questions.explanation: Standard list of food groups.

questions.text: Name three diseases caused by deficiency of nutrients.
questions.answer: Anaemia (lack of iron), scurvy (lack of vitamin C), rickets (lack of vitamin D), and goitre (lack of iodine). Any three are correct.
questions.explanation: Tests memory of common deficiency diseases.

questions.text: Why is a balanced diet important for school children?
questions.answer: School children are still growing and learning. A balanced diet provides energy for play and study, proteins for growth, and vitamins and minerals to keep the body healthy and prevent illness.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of balanced diet importance.

questions.text: Explain how to test a piece of bread for starch.
questions.answer: Place a small piece of bread on a plate. Add 1-2 drops of iodine solution on it. If the bread turns blue-black, it contains starch. Bread does contain starch, so the colour change should be seen.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of the iodine test.

questions.text: Suggest a balanced one-day meal plan for a Class 6 student.
questions.answer: Breakfast: idli/poha + a fruit + milk. Lunch: roti/rice + dal + vegetable + curd + salad. Snack: roasted peanuts or a banana. Dinner: roti/rice + vegetable + dal/paneer + a small bowl of yoghurt. Plenty of water through the day. Many similar plans are acceptable.
questions.explanation: Tests applying balanced-diet principles.

questions.text: A child has been told he has anaemia. Suggest two food items that should be added to his diet and explain why.
questions.answer: Spinach and dal/lentils — both are good sources of iron, which is the mineral in short supply in anaemia. Adding lemon helps absorb the iron better.
questions.explanation: Tests application of nutrition knowledge.

questions.text: A friend says, 'I will eat only chicken because it has protein.' What is wrong with this idea?
questions.answer: Eating only one food, even if it is rich in protein, leaves out other nutrients the body needs — carbohydrates for energy, vitamins and minerals for protection, fibre for digestion. A balanced diet should include foods from all groups.
questions.explanation: Tests analysis of dietary balance.

questions.text: Two children have lunch every day at school. One eats only sugary biscuits; the other eats roti, dal, and a vegetable. Compare the long-term effects on their health.
questions.answer: The child eating only biscuits gets only carbohydrates and a little fat — no proteins, vitamins, or minerals. Over time he may grow more slowly, fall ill more easily, and feel tired. The child eating roti, dal and vegetables gets all major nutrients, helping him grow well, stay active, and have stronger immunity.
questions.explanation: Tests evaluating health outcomes.

questions.text: Plan a one-week meal calendar for a Class 6 student that covers all food groups. Highlight breakfast, lunch, and dinner for each day, and explain how your plan is balanced.
questions.answer: Sample plan (one of many): Mon — Breakfast: poha + banana + milk; Lunch: roti + dal + sabzi + salad + curd; Dinner: rice + rajma + cucumber. Tue — Breakfast: idli + sambar + an orange; Lunch: roti + chana + sabzi + curd; Dinner: rice + dal + palak. Wed — Breakfast: paratha + curd + an apple; Lunch: rice + sambar + boiled egg or paneer + salad; Dinner: roti + sabzi + dal. Thu — Breakfast: upma + a fruit + milk; Lunch: roti + dal + paneer + salad; Dinner: rice + dal + sabzi. Fri — Breakfast: poha + banana + milk; Lunch: roti + dal + sabzi + curd + salad; Dinner: khichdi + raita + papad. Sat — Breakfast: dosa + chutney + a fruit; Lunch: roti + dal + sabzi + salad; Dinner: rice + dal + sabzi. Sun — Breakfast: paratha + curd + a fruit; Lunch: roti + dal + sabzi + raita; Dinner: rice + dal + sabzi. Why balanced: each day has carbohydrates (rice/roti/idli) for energy, proteins (dal/paneer/egg/curd) for growth, fats (in cooking + curd) for sustained energy, vitamins and minerals (sabzi, salad, fruits), fibre (whole grains, salad), and water through curd and meals.
questions.explanation: Open-ended; full credit for any valid balanced plan with explanation.

questions.text: Some children skip breakfast because they wake up late. Discuss why this is harmful and suggest two practical solutions.
questions.answer: Skipping breakfast leaves the body without energy after the long overnight gap, so the child may feel weak, lose concentration, and may overeat later. Over time it can affect growth and learning. Solutions: (1) Sleep on time so waking up early is easier and breakfast time is built in. (2) Keep quick, healthy options ready (boiled eggs, idli, banana with milk) so even on a rushed day a small breakfast is possible. (3) Pack a small mid-morning snack for school to fill the gap if breakfast was small.
questions.explanation: Tests evaluation and providing practical advice.

questions.text: Which of these is a fat-rich food?
questions.explanation: Ghee is concentrated fat from milk.

questions.explanation: Wheat (chapati flour) is a major source of carbohydrates.

questions.text: Why are vitamins called 'protective' nutrients?
options: They help the body fight disease and keep tissues healthy
questions.answer: They help the body fight disease and keep tissues healthy
questions.explanation: Vitamins protect the body and prevent specific deficiency illnesses.

questions.text: You want a quick breakfast that has carbs, protein, and a vitamin. The BEST choice is
options: Poha with peanuts and a fruit
questions.answer: Poha with peanuts and a fruit
questions.explanation: Poha gives carbs, peanuts protein/fat, fruit vitamins.

questions.text: A region has many cases of goitre. The MOST likely reason is
questions.explanation: Iodine deficiency causes goitre and is common where iodised salt is not used.

questions.explanation: Iodised salt provides iodine in daily cooking.

questions.explanation: Iron is a mineral nutrient required for haemoglobin.

questions.text: Calcium is mainly required for the eyes.
questions.explanation: Calcium builds bones and teeth; vitamin A helps eyes.

questions.text: A glass of water has nutrients but no calories.
questions.explanation: Plain water has no calories but is essential for body functions.

questions.text: To check if a food has fat, you can rub a small piece on plain paper and look for a translucent oil patch.
questions.explanation: This is a simple kitchen test for fat.

questions.text: Vitamin _____ is needed for healthy eyesight.
questions.explanation: Vitamin A supports vision; deficiency causes night blindness.

questions.explanation: Calcium builds bones and teeth.

questions.text: To increase iodine in our diet, we should use _____ salt.
questions.explanation: Iodised salt has small amounts of iodine added.

questions.text: Cooking vegetables for too long can destroy some _____, especially vitamin C.
questions.explanation: Heat can destroy heat-sensitive vitamins like vitamin C.

questions.text: Why should we drink clean water?
questions.answer: Clean water keeps the body hydrated and removes waste. Dirty water can carry germs that cause illnesses such as cholera and diarrhoea.
questions.explanation: Highlights both nutrition and hygiene aspects.

questions.text: Suggest two snacks for a school break that are tasty AND healthy.
questions.answer: Roasted chana with chopped fruit; idli with chutney; peanut–jaggery laddu; banana with a glass of milk. Any two reasonable, balanced snacks accepted.
questions.explanation: Tests practical food choices.

questions.text: Which deficiency would you suspect in a child whose gums bleed easily and skin gets bruised? Why?
questions.answer: Vitamin C deficiency, which causes scurvy. Symptoms include bleeding gums and slow healing.
questions.explanation: Tests connecting symptom to deficiency.

questions.text: Should children eat junk food once in a while? Justify your answer.
questions.answer: Eating junk food once in a while is okay if the rest of the diet is balanced. The problem is making junk food a regular meal — it gives extra calories, fat, and salt without proteins, vitamins, or fibre. Moderation matters more than complete avoidance.
questions.explanation: Tests balanced reasoning, not extreme positions.

questions.text: Design a poster (in words) for your school canteen that promotes healthy eating. Include three key messages and three healthy food choices to recommend.
questions.answer: Sample poster: TITLE: Eat Smart, Grow Strong! MESSAGES: (1) Fill half your plate with fruits and vegetables. (2) Drink plenty of clean water and avoid sugary drinks. (3) Pick whole-grain options like roti and brown rice. RECOMMENDED CHOICES: roasted chana with cucumber slices; banana with peanut chikki; idli with sambar and a fruit. Any creative, accurate poster is acceptable.
questions.explanation: Open-ended creative task; checks practical application.

questions.text: You see chips and a banana. Which is the BETTER snack and why?
options: Banana, because it provides vitamins, minerals, and fibre with natural sweetness
questions.answer: Banana, because it provides vitamins, minerals, and fibre with natural sweetness
questions.explanation: Whole fruits are far more nutritious than salty fried snacks.

questions.text: Which slogan BEST captures the idea of balanced eating?
options: Eat a rainbow on your plate
questions.answer: Eat a rainbow on your plate
questions.explanation: Variety of colourful foods often signals a balanced mix of nutrients.

questions.text: Adding lemon to fish curry can help the body absorb iron from the meal.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C in lemon enhances iron absorption.

questions.text: Foods high in vitamin _____ help build immunity and heal wounds.
questions.explanation: Vitamin C supports immunity and collagen formation.

questions.text: What does it mean to eat 'mindfully'?
questions.answer: Mindful eating means paying attention to the food, eating slowly, chewing well, noticing tastes, and stopping when comfortably full instead of overeating.
questions.explanation: Tests understanding of mindful eating.
